name: Ask the user by email: was this you?
description: When an identity alert names a user, emails them "was this you?". Yes dismisses the alert; no, or no answer within an hour, promotes it into a high case grouped by user.
trigger_filter: (alert.source == 'okta' and ((alert.payload.get('actor') or {}).get('alternateId') or '') != '') or (alert.source == 'entra-id' and (alert.payload.get('userPrincipalName') or '') != '') or (alert.source == 'm365-defender' and (alert.payload.get('evidence') or []) | selectattr('userAccount', 'defined') | map(attribute='userAccount') | select | selectattr('userPrincipalName', 'defined') | map(attribute='userPrincipalName') | select | list | length > 0)
setup:
## Before you start
- This server must send email (`SMTP_HOST`, `SMTP_FROM_EMAIL`, see the configuration guide) and `FRONTEND_URL` must be the address users can open: the email links to `/verify/<token>` there.
- The user gets one email with an **Answer** button. Opening the page records nothing (mail scanners open links); the user picks an answer there. The link works once and expires with the question (1 hour; change `timeout_hours` on the ask step, up to 168).

## How it works
- An Okta, Entra ID Protection or Microsoft 365 Defender alert that names a user asks that user **"{{ alert.title }} (reported by {{ alert.source }}). Was this you?"** with two answers: *It was me* or *It wasn't me*.
- *It was me*: the alert is dismissed with the user's confirmation as the reason.
- *It wasn't me*, or no answer before the time limit: the alert is promoted into a **high** case grouped by user (24 hours), with a note saying what the user answered. Nothing is closed on silence.
- Use it **instead of** *Identity alerts: group by user into a case* for the same sources, or disable one of them: both act on the same alerts.
- Pair it with a containment workflow (manual, on the case) rather than containing on a *No* automatically: a user who clicks the wrong button shouldn't lock themselves out.

## Caveats
- The question goes to the address the alert names; an attacker who controls that mailbox or Slack account could answer *Yes*. Keep it for low-to-medium alerts and use suppression rules or containment guardrails for the rest.
- The alert title is shown to the user as plain text.

config.email: {{ ((alert.payload.get('actor') or {}).get('alternateId') if alert.source == 'okta' else (alert.payload.get('userPrincipalName') if alert.source == 'entra-id' else ((alert.payload.get('evidence') or []) | selectattr('userAccount', 'defined') | map(attribute='userAccount') | select | selectattr('userPrincipalName', 'defined') | map(attribute='userPrincipalName') | select | first | default('')))) or '' }}
config.message: {{ alert.title }} (reported by {{ alert.source }}). Was this you?

config.reason: Confirmed by the user ({{ steps.ask.output.responder_email or 'unknown' }})

config.title: Unconfirmed activity: {{ alert.title }}
config.group_key: user:{{ ((alert.payload.get('actor') or {}).get('alternateId') if alert.source == 'okta' else (alert.payload.get('userPrincipalName') if alert.source == 'entra-id' else ((alert.payload.get('evidence') or []) | selectattr('userAccount', 'defined') | map(attribute='userAccount') | select | selectattr('userPrincipalName', 'defined') | map(attribute='userPrincipalName') | select | first | default('')))) or '' }}

config.content: User verification for alert #{{ alert.id }}: {{ 'no answer within the time limit' if steps.ask.output.timed_out else 'the user answered "' ~ steps.ask.output.response ~ '"' }}.
